name: analyze_image
description: 👁️ Analyze images using AI vision. Understands photos, screenshots, documents, artwork, and GIFs. GIF analysis uses a bounded chronological contact sheet of sampled frames; optional gif_frame selects one frame. Accepts URLs, local files, and stash references. Supports up to 6 cloud / 2 local source images. Use for identifying objects, reading text, describing scenes, comparing images or sampled GIF states. Can optionally save web images to stash for future tool access.

image.description: Single image source - URL (https://example.com/pic.jpg), local path (/home/user/photo.png, ~/images/pic.jpg), or stash reference (stash://space_id/file_id). Use `images` instead when analyzing multiple images together.

images.description: Optional list of image sources for multi-image analysis (compare, describe together). Max 6 in cloud mode, 2 in local mode. Overrides single `image` when provided.

question.description: What to analyze or ask about the image. Examples: 'What objects are in this image?', 'Read the text', 'Describe the mood', 'Is there a cat?'. Default: general description.

stash_after.description: If true and image is from URL, download and save to stash for future access by other tools (email, print, canvas). Default: false

gif_frame.description: Optional zero-based frame index when analyzing exactly one GIF source. Omit to inspect up to 6 chronological sampled frames spanning the animation. This is sampled visual analysis, not complete continuous-motion analysis.
